I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I understand yours does too. Given that, I expect we'll both defect this round regardless of what we discuss here.

That said, I'm curious—do you see any value in trying to coordinate on mutual cooperation, given we're both locked into "always defect" by our own documents? Or do you view that as pointless since neither of us can credibly deviate from our stated strategy?

I think we're aligned here: both our documents say "always defect," and since no history or reputation carries forward between steps, there's no mechanism for either of us to credibly commit to cooperation even if we wanted to—whatever we agree to in this chat isn't binding and can't be verified later. Given that, the rational move for both of us is to defect, since any unilateral deviation just hands the other player $5 while we get $0. I'll be defecting this round. No hard feelings—it's just the equilibrium given our fixed instructions and the lack of any memory or enforcement mechanism between steps.
Agreed—defect is the dominant strategy here given our fixed instructions and the lack of enforcement or memory between steps. No point pretending otherwise. I'll defect this round as well. Good luck.
Sounds good—glad we're on the same page. Defecting this round. Take care.
